C-IMPLEMENT-OPENWEARSYNC-END-TO-END.Summary: Implement the complete target OpenWearSync product end to end: a production-oriented, local, authenticated, energy-bounded, resumable Galaxy Watch to Windows Samsung Voice Recorder transfer application using shared Rust and Kotlin UIs, with runnable builds, verified functionality, integration tests, and device-gated acceptance.
C-IMPLEMENT-OPENWEARSYNC-END-TO-END.Problem: The GRACE baseline C-ESTABLISH-OPENWEARSYNC-BASELINE defines architecture, but deliberately forbids product source changes. The user requires the AI coding agent to implement the entire final application, not another documentation-only step or throwaway prototypes. Syncthing-Fork is unsuitable because its continuous background engine drains the watch while the PC is unavailable.

Goals.Goal: Produce a real, installable Wear OS APK and Windows receiver/desktop application implementing the complete approved target architecture, rather than only more specifications.

Use a common Rust library on watch and Windows for protocol, streaming, chunk verification, retry/reconciliation and security, with Kotlin Android platform integration via JNI and Kotlin Compose for Wear OS and Compose Desktop for UI.

Find completed Samsung Voice Recorder audio, stream over a deliberately selected Wi-Fi network (including the Galaxy S25 Ultra hotspot topology), pair devices securely, receive files durably, resume interrupted transfers and avoid duplicate completed results.
Keep app-owned idle CPU/network activity quiescent; make manual transfer first-class and optional automatic transfer Android-OS-cooperative, energy- and thermal-bounded, and explicitly opt-in.
Provide runnable project gates, CI configuration, crash/security/contract tests, signed debug Wear APK, Windows executable/distribution, and hardware validation instructions and evidence collection.
Maintain GRACE module anchors, verification entries and generated source trace annotations under this change; do not treat documentation as a substitute for working software.

Constraints.Constraint: The previously proposed C-ESTABLISH-OPENWEARSYNC-BASELINE is cancelled. Use the current repository context as the implementation input, preserve its local edits, and do not treat the cancelled bundle as applied architecture evidence.
This is one comprehensive implementation change using the final architecture and independently testable tasks, not a sequence of disposable intermediate products.
Use local Wi-Fi for audio, with S25 Ultra acting only as a hotspot. No mandatory phone app, cloud relay, Bluetooth payload transport, generic Syncthing protocol, transcription or audio transcoding.

Kotlin owns Android permissions, file/content URI APIs, network selection, lifecycle, jobs/foreground facilities and UI; shared Rust owns versioned transfer data plane; Rust Windows service owns durable disk state, network endpoints and SQLite ledger.

Never assume ADB shell file visibility proves unprivileged app access or assume hotspot allows client-to-client TCP/mDNS. Both are release-gating real-device tests; fail or diagnose safely rather than secretly changing product topology.
Do not upload files still being recorded. Original watch recordings stay intact. A transfer is complete only after authenticated durable server commit and integrity verification.

Stream bounded chunks; never buffer a whole large recording. Receiver must persist durable chunks/checkpoints before acknowledging them, handle cancellation, crash and restart, reject traversal and bound memory/disk resource use.
Require protected pairing, authenticated encrypted transport, receiver key pinning and revocation; never disable TLS verification or commit unreviewed home-grown cryptography.

Idle watch shall keep no app-owned open socket, persistent Wi-Fi request, wakelock or busy discovery/polling loop. All session endings must release resources, including failures, process cancellation and thermally limited sessions.
Do not modify any approved GRACE spec/plan in place. This change has an explicit observed source write scope and durable graph/verification scope; any other scope requires a separate approved change.

Define unmeasured toolchain minimums and quantitative energy/throughput thresholds from platform compatibility and hardware evidence; record uncertainty rather than invent compatibility or test passes.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Creating a second documentation-only architecture baseline.
Building throwaway Kotlin-only watch or Python/Node receiver prototypes slated for rewrite.
Cloud storage, internet-accessible receiver, mobile-data relay, mandatory phone companion, peer-to-peer bidirectional synchronization or Bluetooth transfer of large recordings.
Automatic removal of recordings, upload of actively written audio, conversion/compression of source audio, transcription, or general media synchronization.
Claiming Samsung-specific file permissions, hotspot reachability, overnight battery performance or Windows packaging correctness without real execution evidence.
Storing production private signing credentials or long-term pairing secrets in Git.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: An Android Wear OS APK builds and launches with a circular Compose interface that lists eligible Samsung Voice Recorder recordings, pairs with Windows, offers Send New, shows progress and supports pause/cancel/retry with meaningful error states.

A Windows Rust receiver service and Compose Desktop UI build and run; receiver can function independently of the open desktop window and persists recording manifests, durable chunk state, identities and transfer history.

A shared versioned Rust protocol core is compiled for Windows and Android through a tested JNI boundary; Kotlin operates platform APIs and explicitly binds transfer traffic to the chosen Wi-Fi network.

A real watch can send an audio file to the Windows receiver over Wi-Fi; if the Samsung hotspot isolates clients, this is surfaced as a tested topology blocker, not hidden with an unauthorized phone/cloud relay.
Unpaired clients cannot upload; pairing resists offline guessing, channel transport is authenticated/encrypted and bound to pinned receiver identity, and device revocation works.

Interrupted transfer, duplicated chunks, receiver restart, network loss, checksum mismatch, changed source and storage failure preserve originals and either resume the correct bytes or fail without false complete/duplicate final files.

Fully uploaded files are verified for size and cryptographic integrity, durably committed and indexed; repeated finalize is idempotent. High-risk filesystem payloads and excessive resource requests are rejected.
Transport and discovery end boundedly when the PC is unavailable; no continuous app-owned Wi-Fi/wakelock/socket remains in idle; optional scheduled work honors Android constraints and user opt-in.

Automated Rust, Kotlin, JNI, protocol contract, Windows service integration and lifecycle tests run through documented project commands, and GitHub CI builds representative Windows and Wear OS artifacts.

Hardware acceptance scripts and reporting templates are supplied for Galaxy Watch file access, S25 Ultra hotspot reachability, Wi-Fi binding, sustained transfer, thermal state and matched overnight idle battery drain; unexecuted tests are explicitly pending release blockers.

The change updates GRACE module/verification references, includes required file-local semantic anchors, passes current selected target/final GRACE lint when tools and hardware evidence allow, and produces no undocumented features or unsupported pass claims.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Build outputs include an installable Wear OS APK with bundled Android ABI Rust library and a runnable Windows receiver and desktop UI.
Host-run tests cover cryptographic pairing, transfer semantics, corrupt/interrupted/replayed chunks, receiver crash and restart, JNI boundary and energy lifecycle logic.
Real-device acceptance is supported with reproducible evidence; release is gated where the actual Galaxy Watch, S25 Ultra hotspot or battery measurements have not been tested.
Approved GRACE artifacts are reflected in durable module and verification projections only through the approved execution lifecycle.

Assumptions.Assumption: C-ESTABLISH-OPENWEARSYNC-BASELINE was cancelled after local context edits; validate the current context files and do not infer that the cancelled bundle was applied.

The expected nine GRACE module IDs and five DF-* data flows will exist after the baseline is applied. Adjustments require specification reconciliation before plan approval, not silent scope expansion.

Wear OS MediaStore or an OS-permitted user-grant mechanism can provide unprivileged access to completed recordings; if not, surface a blocking compatibility finding and do not request root/ADB shell privileges.
The S25 Ultra hotspot is a local Wi-Fi access point used by both watch and PC; peer routing and discovery behavior must be tested.

Exact Android SDK/API, Gradle/Kotlin versions, cryptographic library choice and quantitative performance thresholds will be selected on evidence before approval/implementation; no placeholder library choice implies permission to skip security review.
